attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-16
attempts.entry_title: CA1 place cells and network coordination in Fmr1-null mice (Talbot et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: Fmr1-null place cells resembled wild-type ones on single-cell measures, as the paper reports, but most evidence for discoordinated network discharge did not hold up here. Weaker pass-by-pass covariance between Fmr1-null place cell pairs held, though not at the paper's values; weaker Kendall correlations at gamma and theta timescales, less recurrent network states and weaker ensemble coordination during arena rotation were not seen. Spatial firing quality differed by genotype, mostly in interneurons. No isolation measures or waveforms are given, so all sorted clusters stood in for the paper's well-isolated cells. Slice physiology, LFP phase coupling and the link to place avoidance could not be tested, as those recordings were not deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Talbot, Sparks, Dvorak, Curran, Alarcon and Fenton (2018) that can be tested on CRCNS hc-16, which holds CA1 spike trains with tracked positions from 8 wild-type and 7 Fmr1-null mice in a large box and a stationary and rotating circular arena. It compares cell classes, place cell properties, overdispersion, pass-by-pass covariance, Kendall correlations, locomotion and frame-specific positional information between genotypes. The slice recordings, LFP, sleep recordings and avoidance sessions of the paper are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Of 1,115 clusters, 499 came from 12 WT and 616 from 9 Fmr1-null mice; 226 WT and 334 Fmr1-null well-isolated cells formed the data set.
outcomes.source: Results, Non-spatial and Spatial Single-Cell Discharge Features, paragraph 1; Table S2
outcomes.quote: Of the 1,115 single-unit waveform clusters that were identified, 499 were recorded from 12 WT mice and 616 were recorded from 9 Fmr1-null mice (Table S2) ... 226 WT and 334 Fmr1-null presumptive cells comprised the dataset
outcomes.notes: The data set holds 8 WT mice (M1, M3, M11, M16, M28, M32, M35, M36) and 7 Fmr1-null mice (M9, M10, M18, M29, M33, M34, M37) of the paper's 12 (or 11) and 9, so it is a subset and its counts cannot test the paper's. The well-isolated cells cannot be selected either, as no isolation measure is given (metadata_insufficient). For the record, the cluster counts are within 10% of 499 and 616 only when every session is counted on its own with cluster 0 included (490 WT, 557 Fmr1-null), which with 15 of 21 mice is a coincidence; counted once per cut file without cluster 0 they are 203 and 294.
deviations: Clusters are counted from the file names; the paper's isolation criterion cannot be applied.

outcomes.statement: A lower proportion of the well-isolated cells is classified as interneurons in WT (28, 12.4%) than in Fmr1-null mice (98, 29.3%).
outcomes.source: Results, Non-spatial and Spatial Single-Cell Discharge Features, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: A lower proportion of these were classified as interneurons in WT mice (28, 12.4%) than Fmr1-null mice (98, 29.3%; test of proportions z = 9.4, p = 10�17)
outcomes.notes: Interneurons (rate above 2 AP/s) are 68 of 203 WT clusters (33.5%) and 106 of 238 Fmr1-null clusters (44.5%) in R1, and 35.4% and 48.5% in R2; with the classified cells as denominator 38.6% to 41.4% and 51.7% to 55.7%. Every percentage is far outside 12.4 +/- 1.24 and 29.3 +/- 2.93. The direction holds under every reading and is significant in the main ones (R1 z = -2.36, p = 0.018; R2 z = -3.33, p = 0.0009); with the refractory filter (clusters with at most 0.5% of ISIs below 2 ms) p = 0.092 in R1 and 0.023 in R2. The effect is present but the percentages are not the paper's, so partially reproduced. Only 70 of 774 clusters have more than 0.5% of ISIs below 2 ms and the filter changes the percentages by at most 4.9 points, so this filter does not remove the excess. It is a weak proxy for the isolation measures (interneuron rates are still 4.34 and 6.95 AP/s at the median in R1), so whether poorly isolated clusters explain the excess cannot be told from these data.
deviations: The data set has no isolation measures (IsoIBG, IsoINN) or waveforms, so every sorted cluster other than cluster 0 is used in place of the paper's well-isolated cells, and cells are classified by rate and bursting without waveform width.

The session that classifies a cell ('standard recordings') is open; R1 (each cell from its first stationary session) and R2 (each stationary session on its own) are both run, and a cluster name within a day's cut file is taken as one cell.
Rate alone and rate with bursting give the same interneurons, as the rate decides it.
A refractory filter (at most 0.5% of ISIs below 2 ms, a standard choice) is shown as a proxy for the isolation measures the data set lacks.

outcomes.notes: The square enclosure of the paper's comparison is not recorded with the arena here. outcomes.statement: Overdispersion is lower (spatial firing more reliable) in Fmr1-null mice when the unit is a pass through a place field (variance 4.89 against 5.81).
outcomes.source: Results, Reduced Spatial Discharge Coordination, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Overdispersion was lower (spatial firing was more reliable) in Fmr1-null mice when the unit of analysis is a pass through a place field
outcomes.notes: R2, consecutive 5 s intervals. 12,802 WT and 18,521 Fmr1-null passes, variance of z 3.69 and 3.55 (expected 5.81 and 4.89). The F test finds WT larger (F = 1.04, one-sided p = 0.008) but Levene's test does not (p = 0.998). In R1 the Fmr1-null variance is the larger (3.83 against 3.53). With a 1 s step, F one-sided p = 0.007 and Levene p = 0.61. With the count rule (exp at least the average rate x 5 s, 33% of intervals pass) R2 gives 5,442 and 8,250 passes, variances 5.28 and 4.66, both within tolerance, F = 1.13 (one-sided p < 0.0001) and Levene p = 0.0006, which meets the criterion (the WT pass count is outside 6,776 +/- 678); in R1 it gives Fmr1-null the larger variance (5.16 against 5.00). The outcome stays on the claims file's literal rule; the rule is asked of a reader. Under the literal rule neither the refractory filter (variances 3.71 and 3.55, Levene p = 0.86) nor the code's 32 x 32 grid (3.73 and 3.73, F one-sided p = 0.49) changes the result. Under the count rule the filter leaves both variances within tolerance (Levene p = 0.0004); on the grid variances (5.34, 4.89) and pass counts (6,712, 9,607) are within tolerance, F one-sided p = 0.0001, but Levene p = 0.052.

outcomes.statement: Kendall correlations between Fmr1-null place cell spike trains are weaker than between WT ones at the 25 ms, 40 ms and 125 ms timescales, but not significantly at 1 s and 5 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Reduced Spatial Discharge Coordination, paragraph 3; Figure 4C and 4D
outcomes.quote: At the 25 ms (Figures 4C and 4D) and 40 ms timescales of gamma oscillations, as well as the 125 ms timescale of theta oscillations, Fmr1-null cell pair discharge correlations (n = 504 pairs) were significantly weaker than those of WT cell pairs
outcomes.notes: Eight readings (K1, K2 x whole session, first 5 min x R1, R2); none gives p < 0.05 at 25, 40 or 125 ms (smallest p 0.24). K1, whole session, R2 (122 WT, 210 Fmr1-null pairs) gives mean tau at 25 ms 0.029 against 0.0067, Mann-Whitney p = 0.87, 0.67 and 0.60 at 25, 40 and 125 ms, and p = 0.049 at 1 s and 0.0012 at 5 s, the reverse of the claimed pattern. findings.statement: The data set holds part of the paper's data. It has 8 of 12 WT and 7 of 9 Fmr1-null mice, the large box and the stationary and rotating arena, but no small box or ring sessions, no sleep or quiet-wakefulness recordings, no LFP, no slice recordings and no avoidance sessions. Fourteen of the 32 claims cannot be tested, one of them (the mouse and cell counts) because the data set is a subset.

No isolation measures (IsoIBG, IsoINN), waveforms or cell classes are given, and the files hold every sorted cluster, including cluster 0 (the unsorted spikes of each tetrode). The TS headers hold only the sampling rate, the first timestamp and a track-to-map scale of 1.00. The paper's 226 WT and 334 Fmr1-null well-isolated cells cannot be selected; Table S2 lists fewer cells per session than the files hold clusters (15 against 50 for M16 in stationary arena 1).

Positions are in tracker pixels (0 to 255) with no spatial scale in the data descriptor or the files. The tracked extent of the large box is about 186 pixels in most sessions, about 218 in three (M9, M10, M11) and 188 x 207 in M1, so the scale also differs between sessions.

The header's SAMPLING_INTERVAL and FIRST_TIMESTAMP do not give the times of the position samples. Spikes lie up to 118 samples (about 4 s) after the nominal time of the sample they are filed under, as the stated rate drifts against the spike clock and frames are dropped. The data descriptor's example header gives 58.3 samples/s, where every file has 30.0.

Six spike trains have one backward step in their spike times, of 0.2 to 1.4 s (M34 041015 blackbox P0C2 and P2C2, M37 051115 stationary1 P2C2 and P8C2, M16 090414 rotating P1C1, M35 040215 stationary2 P0C2).

Nothing identifies a cell across sessions. Sessions of a day mostly share a cut file and cluster names, which the attempt takes to be the same cells, but M29 stationary arena 1 and M34 stationary arena 2 have their own cut files, and box and arena sessions are on different days with different cut files.

The _0-15min and _15-30min files repeat the full-session files except one position sample at the split, which is in neither part (M16 090414 rotating, 26,981 + 27,007 samples against 53,989), so a spike filed under it is lost (one of five spike trains checked). The .times files repeat the TS spike times (107 of 107 checked).

disagreements.reason: The deposit holds 8 WT and 7 Fmr1-null mice (confirmed from the zip listing), against 12 and 9 in the paper, so the counts cannot be checked from a subset; the claim is data_missing, not a mismatch. The cells (226 and 334) need isolation measures. The cluster match (490 and 557) appears only when cluster-0 noise files are counted, which is a coincidence.

WT is lower and the difference is significant (R1 p = 0.018, R2 p = 0.0009). The percentages are far outside tolerance under every reading (WT 33.5 to 41.4% against 12.4%; Fmr1-null 44.5 to 55.7% against 29.3%). All non-zero clusters are used with no isolation criteria and interneuron means only rate above 2 AP/s; the interneuron fraction is roughly three times the paper's for WT.

Room frame Fmr1-null is higher with p = 0.012 under reading B (10 and 8 cells) but p = 0.21 under reading A (9 and 7 cells). Under B the arena frame is equally significant (p = 0.02), so the "only marginally" contrast is not seen. There are 3 mice per genotype, against the paper's 20 and 31 cells, and the paper does not say which session classifies the cells. ipos_series counts the 10-visit minimum per 133 ms interval; the code counts it per position sample.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. Which recording classifies a cell as a place cell, interneuron or non-spatial cell ('standard recordings')? For the rotating-arena cells of Figures 5 and S6, are place cells those classified in the stationary session of the same day or in the rotating session's room frame? With same-day stationary classification room-frame Ipos is greater in Fmr1-null (p = 0.012); with rotating-session classification it is not (p = 0.25). For Figure S6 the environment effect on coherence is p = 0.0012 and 0.067. The attempt assumed the stationary session for Figure S6 and judged Figure 5B on both.

Question for the paper's authors. Which recordings enter the locomotion test of Figure S5B (genotype x half ANOVA, 27 error degrees of freedom), and are environments pooled? Pooling the large box and stationary arena recordings gives no interaction (p = 0.67 with 34 recordings, 0.32 with 15 mice), but within each environment the interaction is significant in opposite directions (large box p = 0.021, stationary arena p = 0.0076). The attempt assumed pooling.

entries.name: talbot-2018
entries.title: CA1 place cells and network coordination in Fmr1-null mice (Talbot et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Talbot, Sparks, Dvorak, Curran, Alarcon and Fenton (2018) that can be tested on CRCNS hc-16, which holds CA1 spike trains with tracked positions from 8 wild-type and 7 Fmr1-null mice in a large box and a stationary and rotating circular arena. It compares cell classes, place cell properties, overdispersion, pass-by-pass covariance, Kendall correlations, locomotion and frame-specific positional information between genotypes. The slice recordings, LFP, sleep recordings and avoidance sessions of the paper are not in the data set.
